study: GR00T N1.5 denoise-steps sweep, PyTorch eager e2e (RTX 5090)
clocks_pinned: locked SM 2700 / MEM 14001 MHz (nvidia-smi -lgc/-lmc); measured under load 2692 MHz, 13801 MHz
input_provenance: recorded (simulated) GR1 observations from NVIDIA demo_data/robot_sim.PickNPlace, not synthetic data: 5 episodes [0, 20, 40, 60, 80] x 3 seeds [0, 1, 2]; latency on ds[0]
scope: policy.get_action() full e2e (transforms+ViT+LLM+DiT; the video frames are already decoded by the dataset loader), PyTorch eager, warm
reference_note: 64 steps = near-converged (NOT exact); Euler error ~C/N, so 16 steps is itself ~1% from the infinite-step limit

latency_decomposition.note: eager PyTorch; per-step is the DiT flow-matching pass; intercept is denoise-independent SEE+READ+THINK+prep

deviation_1overN_fit.note: Euler truncation decays ~1/N; there is no saturation knee in the metric — it is a cost/benefit trade vs the linear latency

noise_floor.deviation_replication: 5 episodes x 3 seeds = 15 samples per step (mean±std)

metric_span: Latency: full policy.get_action() wall (transforms+ViT+LLM+DiT on already-decoded frames), PyTorch EAGER -- the relative denoise law; the deployable compiled latency is the full-TensorRT sweep. Deviation: trajectory rel-MAE of the 26-DOF x 16-step action vs a 64-step near-converged reference, matched noise.
